question: Find the value of 47−⁸ ÷ 47³ × 47−¹⁹
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the BODMAS rule, division is performed before multiplication.

Using exponent laws directly: am ÷ aⁿ × ap = am − ⁿ ⁺ p

Expression = 47−⁸ − ³ ⁺ ⁽−¹⁹⁾

Expression = 47−¹¹ − ¹⁹

Expression = 47−³⁰

**∴ The correct answer is 47−³⁰.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

47−⁸ ÷ 47³ × 47−¹⁹

**Formula Used:**

am ÷ aⁿ = am − ⁿ

am × aⁿ = am ⁺ ⁿ

**Calculations:**

Applying the BODMAS rule, we evaluate the division first:

⇒ (47−⁸ ÷ 47³) × 47−¹⁹

⇒ 47−⁸ − ³ × 47−¹⁹

⇒ 47−¹¹ × 47−¹⁹

Now, perform the multiplication using the product rule of exponents:

⇒ 47−¹¹ ⁺ ⁽−¹⁹⁾

⇒ 47−¹¹ − ¹⁹

⇒ 47−³⁰

**∴ The correct answer is 47−³⁰.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It dictates the standard order of mathematical operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. In the absence of brackets, division must be performed before multiplication.

Quotient Rule of Exponents

When dividing two exponential expressions with the exact same base, you subtract the exponent of the denominator from the exponent of the numerator: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying two exponential expressions with the exact same base, you simply add their exponents together: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

Negative Exponent Rule

A negative exponent means taking the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive opposite of the given exponent: a−m = 1 ÷ am
